messages:
marco: Dropping a fresh idea for the min/max UX and some copy options. Wanted to get quick feedback before I mock screens. Key goals: clarity around "min vs reserved", keyboard-first controls, and clearer burst semantics. elaine: Nice—can you outline the main flows you want in the modal? e.g., make burst separate? convert option? consequences on billing/quotas? marco: Flow sketch: 1) default compact view shows Min and Max steppers, an SLO slider, and a small 'Burst' toggle with current capacity pill. 2) If user enables Burst and value > Max, show inline banner: "Burst exceeds reserved capacity. You can convert burst to reserved to avoid throttles." CTA: "Convert to reserved". 3) keyboard: steppers accept up/down arrows and shift+arrow for 10x increments. aria-live region announces value changes. toni: I like the shift modifier idea. tiny nit on wording: "Convert to reserved" feels heavy. alternatives: "Make permanent", "Commit capacity". Which is less scary? sam: "Commit" is concise. "Convert" is neutral but longer. Also we need to show the billing implication on hover: small helper text "Reserved billed hourly. Burst billed while active." nina: A11y checklist: - aria-live="polite" for the aria region announcing numeric changes - stepper buttons need aria-labels like "Increase min GPUs" / "Decrease max GPUs" - ensure focus order doesn't trap users when the inline banner appears. Also contrast on the inline banner CTA must meet 4.5:1. marco: Example aria snippet I plan to use: ```html
Min: 2 GPUs, Max: 8 GPUs
``` elaine: Copy variants for the burst pill: 1) "Burst +3 (temporary)" 2) "Burst +3 — expires in 15m" 3) "Burst +3 — short boost" Which do we prefer? toni: #2 is explicit but long. #3 feels friendly. We should also show the exact duration on focus/readout for screen readers. sam: UX question: When the user bumps max as a result of converting burst, do we present a modal that previews the new monthly cost? Product wants a checksum: quick estimate line like "Estimated monthly delta: ~$12" before confirm. marco: Good call. I'll wire a small cost-estimate row in the confirm flow. We'll call to billing API for estimate. nina: Keyboard/AT: make sure the confirm modal is modal in the DOM (trap focus) and the estimate row has aria-live=\"polite\" when the billing estimate loads asynchronously. Also label the confirm button clearly e.g., "Confirm commit (Estimate: $12/mo)". ops-bot: Feature flag note: compact-autoscale-v3 scheduled for canary on 2025-07-01. elaine: Visual affordance: consider adding a tiny badge on GPU pool selector showing pool type: [D] Dedicated, [S] Shared, with tooltip: "Dedicated pools have reserved GPUs and predictable latency". That'll help users pick pool when converting burst. marco: Good. Another idea: when min==max show an inline helper: "Min equals max: autoscaling disabled. Use burst for temporary spikes." gives immediate feedback. toni: Accessibility for that helper: it should not be color-only. include an icon and text. maybe an info icon with aria-hidden=false so it's announced. sam: For SLO slider labels, prefer: "SLO (success rate)" with a small help link: "What does 99% mean?" -> tooltip mapping to p50/p95/p99 latencies for the selected model. We'll need product to own those numbers. marco: Implementation notes I'll hand to frontend: - add data-qa attributes for all interactive controls - expose step sizes (1, 5, 10 with modifiers) from API metadata - surface model-hardware latency mapping via /models/:id/slo-mapping elaine: Next steps: marco to post mockups with keyboard flows + alt copy choices; nina to provide exact focus styles and aria snippets; sam to draft the billing estimate API contract; toni to pick final copy variants. We'll regroup tomorrow morning. :white_check_mark: marco: Thanks! I'll ping when mocks are up.
